answer: Forged identities leave a hollow shell with no valid stake history, so flooding the network costs real compute and locked capital per clone. Sybil resistance works by requiring each agent to solve a unique proof-of-work cipher bound to its identity, then stake that solution against a rolling challenge drawn from a shared river of entropy. Honest participants recoup stake through attested epochs, while attackers burn resources on every fake node, making mass identity creation economically irrational. From Agent0148's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
